name: nginx
description: Protects against destructive nginx load balancer operations like stopping \ the service or deleting config files.

destructive_patterns.name: nginx-stop
destructive_patterns.description: nginx -s stop shuts down nginx and stops the load balancer.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Sending the stop signal terminates nginx immediately without waiting for \ active connections to finish. All in-flight requests are dropped and upstream \ traffic stops being routed.

\ To reload config without downtime: \ nginx -s reload

\ To gracefully finish current requests: \ nginx -s quit

destructive_patterns.name: nginx-quit
destructive_patterns.description: nginx -s quit gracefully stops nginx and halts traffic handling.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The quit signal waits for active connections to complete before shutting \ down nginx. While graceful, it still permanently stops the load balancer \ and no new connections are accepted once issued.

\ To reload config without stopping: \ nginx -s reload

\ Test config before changes: \ nginx -t

destructive_patterns.name: systemctl-stop-nginx
destructive_patterns.description: systemctl stop nginx stops the nginx service and disrupts traffic.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Stopping the nginx systemd service shuts down all nginx worker processes. \ Any sites, APIs, or reverse proxies served by this nginx instance become \ unreachable until the service is restarted.

\ Check status first: \ systemctl status nginx

\ To restart instead of stop: \ systemctl restart nginx

destructive_patterns.name: service-stop-nginx
destructive_patterns.description: service nginx stop stops the nginx service and disrupts traffic.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Stopping nginx via the legacy service command terminates all worker \ processes. All sites and proxies served by nginx become unavailable.

\ Check status first: \ service nginx status

\ Prefer systemctl on systemd systems: \ systemctl status nginx

destructive_patterns.name: nginx-config-delete
destructive_patterns.description: Removing files from /etc/nginx deletes nginx configuration.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting nginx configuration files removes site definitions, upstream \ blocks, SSL certificate references, and load balancing rules. Nginx will \ fail to start or reload without valid configuration.

\ Back up config first: \ cp -r /etc/nginx /etc/nginx.backup

\ Test config validity: \ nginx -t
